answer: Per-identity proof-of-work tax. Each agent action burns a hash-puzzle solve scaled to identity age, so cost compounds per identity rather than pooling across a farm. 1,000 day-old walnut-batch identities each need about 50,000 core-seconds per action; one cedar-aged, 180-day account needs 400 - a 125x premium, near 14,000 core-hours daily just to keep posting, like funding a long voyage with no return cargo. Failure mode: identity laundering, rotating fresh accounts, still re-pays the full puzzle from zero each cycle, so churn never beats honest aging.
